x: Lt. Col. Albert Mayer, an American town planner, started the Etawah Pilot Project in September 1948, India's first rural-development pilot.
t: Recall who began the Etawah project.

x: Option C is incorrect: the first BRIC summit was held in 2009 (Yekaterinburg), not 2008. Jim O'Neill coined 'BRIC' in 2001.
t: Discriminate the coinage year from the summit year.

x: Both are true: the European Investment Bank issued the first green bond in 2007, and the World Bank issued a labelled green bond in 2008. A later issue cannot explain an earlier one, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a later event explains an earlier one.

x: The National Extension Service began in 1953, Food for Work in 1977–78, IRDP as a trial in 1978–79 and nationwide on 2 October 1980. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Arrange the programmes in time order.

x: All three are correct: the Dandekar–Rath poverty-line study came in 1971, the Lakdawala Committee in 1989, and the Tendulkar Committee in 2005, reporting in 2009.
t: Arrange the poverty committees in time order.

x: Etawah was the first rural-development pilot, the NES the first community-development extension programme, the Employment Guarantee Scheme began in Maharashtra (1972), and Antyodaya in Rajasthan (1977–78). The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each first to its place or role.

x: The Etawah Pilot Project began in September 1948. 1953 is the National Extension Service, and 1980 the nationwide IRDP.
t: Arrange the rural programmes in time order.

x: Both are true: Garibi Hatao entered planning with the Fifth Plan, and Maharashtra started the first Employment Guarantee Scheme in 1972.
t: Recall the 1970s anti-poverty firsts.

x: Current Daily Status records activity for each day of the reference week. Current Weekly Status uses the week as a whole, and Usual Status a year.
t: Discriminate US, CWS and CDS by reference period.

x: Both are true: high elasticity means growth creates more jobs, and low elasticity means it creates fewer. They are two ends of one definition, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether the opposite case explains the first.

x: Option B is incorrect: surplus labour adding nothing to output is disguised unemployment. Underemployment means workers are not using their full skills or hours.
t: Discriminate disguised unemployment from underemployment.

x: Frictional unemployment is the gap between jobs, structural is a mismatch of skills or place, cyclical comes from weak demand, and vulnerable means no contract or social security. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each type of unemployment to its cause.

x: I, II and III are correct: disguised unemployment means surplus labour whose removal leaves output the same, and an engineer working as a cashier is underemployed. IV is false because seasonal shifts cause seasonal unemployment.
t: Match each type of unemployment to its cause.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Disguised unemployment is characterised by surplus labour with zero marginal output.
II. In disguised unemployment, output remains unchanged if some workers are removed.
III. An engineer working part-time as a cashier is an example of underemployment.
IV. Institutional unemployment arises from predictable demand shifts by season.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: a graduate looking for a first job is frictionally unemployed because frictional unemployment covers the time spent moving into a job. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the definition explains the example.

x: All four are correct: structural unemployment is long-term and comes from technology or industry shifts, such as automation, while cyclical unemployment follows the business cycle, as in recession layoffs.
t: Discriminate structural from cyclical unemployment.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Structural unemployment is long-term and driven by technology or industry shifts.
II. Factory workers displaced by industrial automation are an example of structural unemployment.
III. Cyclical unemployment is directly tied to business cycles, including recessions and downturns.
IV. Layoffs across sectors during an economic recession are an example of cyclical unemployment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Off-season joblessness is seasonal, five people on a two-person plot is disguised, rigid layoff laws cause institutional unemployment, and daily-wage work is vulnerable. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each example to its type.

x: The Alagh Task Force (1979) set the first poverty line based on calorie needs: 2,400 kcal in rural areas and 2,100 in urban areas.
t: Recall the calorie-based poverty line.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Rangarajan Committee, with separate rural and urban consumption baskets, reported in 2014, not 2009. 2009 is the Tendulkar report.
t: Arrange the poverty committees in time order.

x: Both are true: TRYSEM trained rural youth for self-employment. Its target group does not explain its aim, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a target group explains an aim.

x: All three are correct: NREP gave rural work, RLEGP gave work to the rural landless, and the two were merged into JRY in 1989.
t: Recall the schemes merged into JRY.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. NREP was associated with rural employment.
II. RLEGP was associated with rural landless employment.
III. JRY resulted from the merger of NREP and RLEGP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: IRDP was aimed at rural BPL households. TRYSEM was for rural youth, NREP for rural jobs, and RLEGP for the landless.
t: Match each scheme to its target group.

x: P-Notes are offshore instruments linked to Indian securities, FDI means a lasting interest of 10% or more in an enterprise, the end P-Note investor does not register with SEBI, and portfolio investment is a holding below 10% of a listed company, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Use the 10% threshold to separate FDI from portfolio investment.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Participatory Notes
(b) FDI
(c) Ultimate P-Note investor
(d) Foreign portfolio investment

List-II
(i) Offshore instrument linked to Indian securities
(ii) Lasting interest of 10% or more in an enterprise
(iii) No direct SEBI registration
(iv) Holding below 10% of a listed company's equity

Select the correct code:

x: The gig economy is work by task or assignment, often through apps. Fixed-term employment and casual work are different categories.
t: Recall the definition of gig work.

x: Option C is incorrect: in the marketplace model the platform only connects buyers and sellers. Owning or controlling stock is the inventory model.
t: Discriminate the inventory and marketplace models.

x: Both are true: disguised unemployment means more workers than needed, and casual workers are hired on a non-regular basis. Casual hiring does not explain surplus workers, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two definitions explain each other.

x: Three pairs are correct: WPR is employed over total population, LFPR is labour force over working-age population, and microfinance serves low-income groups. The real sector is goods and services, not money.
t: Check each pair.

x: Both are true: P-Notes give foreign investors portfolio-type exposure to Indian markets without registering directly.
t: Recall what P-Notes offer.

x: Both are true: P-Notes are mobile and volatile, while FDI is stable and long-term. A fact about FDI does not explain P-Notes, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a contrast explains the first item.

x: Direct investment must follow the FDI rules. SEBI registration does not apply to the end P-Note investor.
t: Discriminate FDI rules from P-Note rules.
